when: Hourly at :06, and each time the pacer starts one
does: One unattended cloud session on Opus at effort low: reads your feedback, triages new issues, does tickets (one PR each) and reports each run on the branch metrics; never takes a lane:haiku or lane:deep ticket

when: Only when the pacer starts one (no schedule); a new session each time
does: One unattended cloud session on Haiku: does one lane:haiku ticket (one PR) and stops, so that its prompt stays small; no triage, refill, roadmap or process review
where: Scheduled task “aoe2mc autopilot haiku” (argument max lane haiku), .claude/skills/autopilot

when: Only when the pacer starts one (no schedule); a new session each time
does: One unattended cloud session on Opus at effort high: does the lane:deep tickets (a choice where a wrong answer can pass the tests: an unknown bug cause, a race, a new structure, a change to how the runs plan, a ticket that failed before, large tickets to split), the epic check, the queue refill, the roadmap review and the process review; stops when no lane:deep ticket is ready and the refill is done
where: Scheduled task “aoe2mc autopilot deep” (argument max lane deep), .claude/skills/autopilot/queue.md (Deep lane)

when: A cycle every 10 minutes (GitHub workflow pacer.yml)
does: A script with no Claude session. Reads the 5-hour and 7-day usage and starts 0 to 8 new runs through the API triggers of the tasks, so that usage follows the target: the lane runs (haiku, deep) for their ready tickets and the refill first, then Opus runs

when: Each pacer cycle
does: 90 % of the 5-hour window 2 hours before the reset, then 98 % at the reset; the 7-day window limits it too when week_guard in agent.toml is true (now true). The target counts Opus runs: a lane run counts its weight (agent.toml weights, measured by framework/tools/health.py)

when: When a run writes a ticket, and each pacer cycle
does: The ticket skill gives each ticket the cheapest lane that does it right at the first try: lane:haiku when the body leaves nothing to decide (also when unsure), no label for the main runs, lane:deep when a wrong answer can pass the tests (about 10 to 20 %). The main runs never take a ticket of a reserved lane

when: Each run, a beat every few minutes
does: A run locks its ticket with the ref claim/N and beats it; a claim without a beat for 25 minutes is free again

when: When fewer tickets are ready than runs
does: Makes new tickets from the open epics, at most 2 × runs − ready (12 at most); closes finished epics; only deep runs do it (framework/tools/claim.py --refill)

when: When the epics have no work left; a review once per 2 hours (a lock)
does: Turns the missing features of the three goals into new epics

when: A time-slot lock: one review per 45 minutes; a slot without a large loss doubles (up to 6 hours)
does: Looks at the whole system (how runs start, the loop, time and quota, quality, weak spots, reuse); changes one thing only when a loss is above its threshold, and checks the last change

when: Each run report, and the roadmap review
does: What 100 % means for each goal: the features with milestones B, A and C, the release checks and a 30 % bug reserve

when: Read by each tool
does: The project values (owner, repository, commands, labels) in one file, so that the system can run another project

when: Once, for a new project
does: Copies the generic parts to a new repository and prints the setup steps that only the owner can do

when: When a design has several good options
does: For the runs: a “Decide: …” ticket with the label needs-human; the work that needs it waits. In the owner's session, the agent asks directly

when: Any time
does: Issues and comments by Larspolo; priorities P0 to P3; the label muted parks a ticket; the label paused on the status issue stops all runs

when: Each PR and each push to main
does: Lint (ruff) and the fast tests

when: Each night at 03:17 UTC
does: The slow tests and the tests on a real Minecraft server; a red run opens a P0 ticket

when: After each CI run, and a sweep every 5 minutes
does: Merges a PR when its quick CI is green; skips hold, needs-human and blocked

when: Every 20 minutes
does: Merges main into PRs with a conflict, or labels them conflict; a run merges main in one call with framework/tools/merge_main.py

when: When an issue closes, and daily at 05:53 UTC
does: Deletes the claim refs of closed tickets

when: On issue and PR events, and hourly at :23
does: Updates the dashboard on issue #1 (also the count of muted tickets and process changes)

when: Each push to main
does: Updates docs/coverage.md and the feature table
